skill.name: adaptyv
skill.description: Use Adaptyv to plan and submit protein validation experiments through a cloud laboratory API. The skill covers assay selection, sequence optimization, status tracking, and result retrieval.
skill.summary: Prepare protein validation workflows for Adaptyv cloud laboratory experiments.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The skill is a documented Adaptyv API workflow that uses external HTTP services, local result files, and user-provided API credentials. Most high and critical static hits are placeholders, Markdown fences, or secure credential guidance, not malicious code. A residual privacy risk remains because proprietary protein sequences are submitted to hardcoded external endpoints.

remediation.suggestion: Use official branded API domains where possible, document data handling, and require explicit user confirmation before submitting sequences.

remediation.issue: Local result files use derived experiment identifiers
remediation.suggestion: Sanitize experiment IDs and output directories before writing files, and avoid overwriting existing files without confirmation.

remediation.issue: Credential handling examples use API tokens
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to use least-privilege Adaptyv tokens and never share tokens with unrelated endpoints or prompts.

remediation.issue: Dependency installation is shown in setup commands
remediation.suggestion: Pin trusted package versions and recommend isolated environments before running examples.

content.value_statement: Protein design teams need clear paths from computational candidates to experimental validation. This skill guides Adaptyv assay planning, API submissions, status tracking, and result review.
actual_capabilities: Explains Adaptyv authentication, API endpoints, and required request fields.
Shows workflows for binding, expression, thermostability, and enzyme activity experiments.
Provides examples for submitting experiments, checking status, retrieving results, and batch analysis.
Describes protein optimization with NetSolP, SoluProt, SolubleMPNN, ESM, ipTM, and pSAE.
Includes guidance for FASTA validation, webhooks, retries, rate limits, and credit monitoring.
limitations: Requires external Adaptyv API access and a valid API key.
Submits sequences and metadata to external laboratory services.
Experimental results may take about 21 days and depend on platform availability.
Does not replace scientific review or compliance checks for regulated research.

use_cases.title: Plan Protein Assays
use_cases.description: Select assay types, prepare FASTA inputs, and define metadata before sending candidates for validation.

use_cases.title: Track Laboratory Experiments
use_cases.description: Check experiment status, plan webhook handling, monitor credits, and organize result retrieval.

use_cases.title: Optimize Design Libraries
use_cases.description: Screen and rank protein variants before choosing candidates for wet lab testing.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Submission
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single experiment plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Adaptyv skill to prepare a binding assay submission plan for these FASTA sequences: [paste sequences]. Include required fields.

prompt_templates.title: Check Experiment Progress
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for tracking active experiments.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Adaptyv references to outline how I should check status for experiment IDs [list IDs]. Include retry and webhook guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Candidate Selection
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the protein optimization guidance to rank these protein variants for expression testing: [paste variants]. Explain the screening workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Design an End-to-End Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a full research workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Adaptyv workflow for 200 designed proteins from sequence cleanup through optimization, submission, status tracking, and result analysis.

output_examples.input: I have 12 antibody variants and need a binding assay plan.
output_examples.output: A submission checklist with assay type, target selection, FASTA validation, metadata, webhook choice, and expected result timing.

output_examples.input: My expression results are complete and I need next steps.
output: A summary of expression and quality metrics to compare.
Recommendations for the next design iteration.

output_examples.input: I need to reduce failed submissions for a large variant library.
output_examples.output: A validation workflow covering sequence cleanup, solubility screening, candidate ranking, batching, and credit monitoring.

best_practices: Review sequence confidentiality before sending data to any external service.
Validate FASTA format and metadata before creating experiments.
Use isolated environments and least-privilege API tokens for examples.
anti_patterns: Do not paste production API keys into prompts, tickets, or shared files.
Do not submit proprietary sequences without authorization.
Do not reuse example file paths without checking overwrite risk.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps plan Adaptyv protein validation workflows, API submissions, status checks, and result handling.

faq.question: Does it run experiments by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for using the external Adaptyv cloud laboratory API.

faq.question: Do I need an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. The references state that Adaptyv API access and a bearer token are required.

faq.question: Can it optimize protein sequences?
faq.answer: It explains workflows that use external and local tools for solubility, naturalness, and stability screening.

faq.question: What data leaves my environment?
faq.answer: Examples submit protein sequences, metadata, and authentication headers to external laboratory or prediction services.

faq.question: Is it suitable for regulated research?
faq.answer: Use it only after your own compliance, data handling, and scientific review requirements are satisfied.
